subject: POC Trial environment options — hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Nguyen <alex@acmeai.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Trial environment options — hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC

Thanks for a productive call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps.

Summary of agreed goals (please flag anything missing):
- Success criteria (what Acme AI will evaluate):
  - Latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms for 512-token generations on the target prompt set.
  - Throughput: sustained 20 requests/sec for peak batch tests.
  - Cost: unit token cost target of <= $0.0009/token for eval workload.
  - Quality: pass rate >= 90% on the 120-step prompt regression suite (NPS-style scoring).
- Evaluation plan:
  - Week 0: environment provisioning and test dataset upload.
  - Week 1: smoke tests and latency profiling.
  - Week 2: throughput / load tests and quality/regression runs.
  - Week 3: candidate optimizations (batching/quantization) and final report.
- Ownership:
  - Acme AI: provide test prompts, identify network contact for VPC, and run app-level validation.
  - Redwood: provision environment, baseline configs, run load tests, and share dashboards.

Environment options we discussed (quick pros/cons):
- Hosted (fastest to start): Redwood-hosted trial environment, minimal network work, start within 24-48 hours.
- Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool in Redwood; predictable performance, recommended for sustained throughput validation; provisioning estimate ~10 business days.
- VPC trial (hosted control plane, customer networking): best for security-sensitive teams; requires network review and IP allowlist from Acme; estimate ~2-3 weeks depending on networking calendar.

Ask / next steps:
1) Please confirm which environment you prefer (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC). If VPC, can you share the network contact and preferred maintenance window?
2) Confirm the success criteria above or send edits by EOD Monday.
3) We'll attach a one-page mutual action plan and draft schedule once you confirm environment.

Attachments: trial-plan.pdf (one-page timeline + baseline configs)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m kickoff once you confirm environment.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: POC Trial environment options — hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC

Adding a quick technical breakdown to support the decision. TL;DR: Hosted gets them live fastest with realistic perf for initial quality and latency checks. Dedicated recommended if they want sustained throughput testing or isolation for noisy workloads. VPC has the strongest security posture but adds ops friction.

Provisioning / timeline estimates (approx):
- Hosted: provisioning and baseline config < 48 hours. We provide API keys, sample SDK instructions, and a short runbook. Minimal Redwood-side engineer time (~4 hours) and ~8-12 hours of Acme engineer time to upload prompts and run initial tests.
- Dedicated sandbox: procurement + GPU pool config ~8-10 business days. Redwood setup ~16 engineer hours (includes capacity tuning), Acme time ~2-3 days for validation and test runs.
- VPC trial: depends on network scheduling. Requires IP allowlist, peering/VPN details, and customer security review. Redwood infra onboarding ~24 engineer hours; total calendar ~10-15 business days depending on CISO calendar.

Suggested config for Hosted trial (to meet their stated success criteria quickly):
- Model: open-llama-13b-quant (or similar we verified in catalog) with 8-bit quantization.
- Instance: 2 x A100-equivalent shared nodes with adaptive batching.
- Initial limits: 30rps sustained with 32-token typical prompt, ramp testing to 30rps for 1 hour as requested.

SME notes: If they want to run 30rps with long prompts (500+ tokens), dedicated or larger instance sizes will be necessary to hit the 95p latency SLO.

I can draft the mutual action plan and include the exact run commands we use for the load tests.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC Trial environment options — hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for looping Tom. Based on Dev's notes and your preference to move fast, here's the proposed plan and schedule for a Hosted first-pass trial. I attached a short mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with the timeline below.

Proposed plan (Hosted trial first, option to upgrade to Dedicated sandbox):
- Day 0 (next business day after sign-off): Redwood provisions hosted trial env, provides API keys and baseline runbook.
- Day 1: Acme uploads prompt set (we'll provide upload script). Smoke tests and a 10-15 minute latency profile run.
- Day 3: Throughput run — 30rps sustained for 1 hour (as requested). We will run both 32-token and 512-token profiles; report on 95p latency.
- Day 7-14: Regression/quality runs, iterate on prompt engineering, and apply batching/quantization tuning if needed.
- End of Week 3: Final performance/quality report and recommendation on whether to transition to Dedicated sandbox for sustained load.

Estimated Redwood and Acme effort:
- Redwood: Setup + run tests + report ~24 engineer-hours across Solutions + Infra.
- Acme: Data prep + validation ~8-16 engineer-hours depending on prompt instrumentation.

Deliverables:
- Baseline performance dashboard (token-level cost & latency breakdown)
- Throughput and latency runbooks used for tests
- Final aggregated report with pass/fail on success criteria and next-step recommendations

Next steps / asks from Acme:
1) Confirm: \"Start hosted trial\" by replying with \"CONFIRM — Hosted\"
2) Share the internal security contact for the vendor questionnaire (Tom is already cc'd).
3) Sign the one-page MPA (DocuSign link in related links) to allow provisioning.

If you confirm today, we can target provisioning tomorrow and run the first smoke test on Monday.

Best,
Marissa
